tables.name: Generation mix in the Spanish peninsular electrical system at 12:30 CEST on 28-A-2025
tables.source: Comité 28-A (Informe no confidencial, p. 38); REE Press Office; ENTSO-E Factual Report
tables.note: This snapshot shows the classic low-demand scenario with inverter-renewable dominance that triggered voltage control alerts. Only 18% was synchronous generation, with barely 11 conventional units connected (minimum of 2025).

tables.name: Unavailability of conventional generation by technology, April 28, 2025
tables.source: Informe de Restricciones Técnicas REE (cifras propias) vs Informe Comité 28-A (Tabla 1, p. 20)
tables.note: The discrepancy of 3,028 MW between REE and the Government fuels the debate on whether the system operator had sufficient synchronous capacity. Compass Lexecon/INESC TEC highlights that between 08:00 and 10:00 CET REE disconnected 15 CCGTs.

tables.name: System inertia H_tot on 28-A (seconds)
tables.source: ENTSO-E Factual Report p. 36; REE 18-jun-2025 p. 11

data.valor: "Mayor inercia no habría evitado la pérdida de sincronismo"

tables.note: Confirms that inertia, although low, was NOT the root cause; the problem was voltage control, not inertial RoCoF.

tables.name: Hourly marginal prices OMIE 28-A vs 29-A 2025 (Spain, €/MWh)
tables.source: OMIE Mercado Diario; Infobae; OCU; Grupo ASE
tables.note: The negative price during central hours evidences the context of renewable oversupply; after the blackout, balancing service costs skyrocketed.

tables.name: Pre-blackout international exchange program (MW, exporting)
tables.note: The operator's mitigations reduced flows to improve damping, but by decreasing currents, the lines consumed less reactive power, raising voltages — a critical side effect.

tables.name: Oscillatory modes identified before the collapse
tables.source: REE pp. 3-5; ENTSO-E Factual Report p. 53; Comité 28-A pp. 31-34; arXiv 2511.17433
tables.note: The forced oscillation at 0.63 Hz, possibly originating from a PV plant in Badajoz, was the trigger that activated the mitigation measures which paradoxically degraded voltage control.

tables.name: Frequency evolution and RoCoF during the 27 critical seconds
tables.source: REE pp. 8-12; Comité 28-A pp. 41-58; Compass Lexecon ¶189
tables.note: The final frequency drop (>1.5 Hz/s) exceeds the standard RoCoF protection threshold for synchronous machines.

tables.name: Voltages at critical 400 kV nodes during the cascade (kV)

data.notas: Colector 220 kV: 242,5 kV (1,10 pu) → trip transformador

tables.note: Refutes the 'widespread overvoltage exceeding limits' narrative: in transmission, voltages remained mostly within the 375-435 kV range; the failure was on the 220 kV/collector side.

tables.name: International exchanges minute by minute T-30 to T+30
